Justice Robert Bromwich handed down his decision in the federal court on Tuesday, in the latest chapter of a long-running feud with Ofir Birenbaum, who visited the popular Middle Eastern restaurant wearing a Star of David cap and necklace with reporters from the Daily Telegraph in February 2025. The operation, later revealed to have been dubbed “undercover Jew” internally by the newspaper, made international headlines after it backfired.

In a May hearing over allegations that Birenbaum breached parts of the settlement, lawyers for Cairo Takeaway alleged the statements by Birenbaum and Giles were a “coordinated effort” to discredit the settlement and “control the narrative” in the media. “These were victory statements, they were planned, they were intended to bury the joint statement in the news cycle, and they had that effect,” Matthew Richardson told the court. Birenbaum’s lawyer, Kieran Smark SC, denied the comments were inconsistent with the official joint statement. He also suggested Birenbaum was vindicated because the restaurant had made a public apology.

In August, Birenbaum launched defamation proceedings against the restaurant’s owner, Hesham El Masry, and staff member Talaat Yehia for statements made in a series of social media posts. Birenbaum denied the version of events depicted in the posts, which the restaurant later deleted and apologised for before the defamation suit was launched. The case settled in March, but was reopened after the restaurant alleged Birenbaum had breached parts of the settlement the parties had agreed after he released a personal statement claiming he was “completely vindicated”. His lawyer, Rebekah Giles, also sent statements to the media in which she labelled the settlement “an important win for Ofir Birenbaum and the Australian Jewish community”, the court heard.

original_article.research:
[Lähde: The Guardian World]
Federal court judge rules Ofir Birenbaum breached parts of settlement with Middle Eastern restaurant reached after incident when working with Daily Telegraph

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A pro-Israel activist breached parts of a legal settlement with Sydney restaurant Cairo Takeaway, a court has ruled, after he claimed to have been “completely vindicated” following the settlement.

Justice Robert Bromwich handed down his decision in the federal court on Tuesday, in the latest chapter of a long-running feud with Ofir Birenbaum, who visited the popular Middle Eastern restaurant wearing a Star of David cap and necklace with reporters from the Daily Telegraph in February 2025.

The operation, later revealed to have been dubbed “undercover Jew” internally by the newspaper, made international headlines after it backfired.

In August, Birenbaum launched defamation proceedings against the restaurant’s owner, Hesham El Masry, and staff member Talaat Yehia for statements made in a series of social media posts.

Birenbaum denied the version of events depicted in the posts, which the restaurant later deleted and apologised for before the defamation suit was launched.

The case settled in March, but was reopened after the restaurant alleged Birenbaum had breached parts of the settlement the parties had agreed after he released a personal statement claiming he was “completely vindicated”.

His lawyer, Rebekah Giles, also sent statements to the media in which she labelled the settlement “an important win for Ofir Birenbaum and the Australian Jewish community”, the court heard.

In a May hearing over allegations that Birenbaum breached parts of the settlement, lawyers for Cairo Takeaway alleged the statements by Birenbaum and Giles were a “coordinated effort” to discredit the settlement and “control the narrative” in the media.

“These were victory statements, they were planned, they were intended to bury the joint statement in the news cycle, and they had that effect,” Matthew Richardson told the court.

Birenbaum’s lawyer, Kieran Smark SC, denied the comments were inconsistent with the official joint statement. He also suggested Birenbaum was vindicated because the restaurant had made a public apology.

payload.title: Sydneyläisravintola voitti oikeudessa kiistan aktivistin sovintokommenteista
payload.summary: Australian liittovaltion tuomioistuin on katsonut, että Ofir Birenbaum rikkoi osia sovinnosta, jonka hän oli tehnyt Sydneyssä toimivan Cairo Takeaway -ravintolan kanssa pitkään jatkuneessa kiistassa.
payload.content:
Australian liittovaltion tuomioistuin on katsonut, että Israel-myönteinen aktivisti Ofir Birenbaum rikkoi osia oikeudellisesta sovinnosta, jonka hän oli tehnyt suositun sydneyläisen Cairo Takeaway -ravintolan kanssa. Ratkaisu liittyi Birenbaumin sovinnon jälkeen antamiin lausuntoihin, joissa hän sanoi tulleensa ”täysin oikeutetuksi” kiistan lopputuloksessa.

## Tuomio liittyi sovinnon jälkeisiin lausuntoihin

Tuomari Robert Bromwich antoi ratkaisunsa tiistaina Australian liittovaltion tuomioistuimessa. Asia on jatkoa kiistalle, joka sai alkunsa helmikuussa 2025, kun Birenbaum vieraili Lähi-idän ruokaa tarjoavassa Cairo Takeaway -ravintolassa Daavidin tähdellä varustettu lippalakki ja kaulakoru yllään. Mukana oli Daily Telegraph -lehden toimittajia.

Lehden sisäisesti käyttämäksi nimeksi kerrottu operaatio nousi myöhemmin kansainvälisiin otsikoihin sen jälkeen, kun tapaus kääntyi tekijöitään vastaan. Kiista johti myöhemmin kunnianloukkausmenettelyyn, jonka Birenbaum käynnisti ravintolan omistajaa Hesham El Masrya ja työntekijä Talaat Yehiaa vastaan sosiaalisen median julkaisujen vuoksi.

Birenbaum kiisti julkaisuissa esitetyn version tapahtumista. Ravintola poisti julkaisut ja pyysi niitä anteeksi ennen kunnianloukkauskanteen nostamista.

## Ravintola arvosteli ”voitonjulistuksia”

Asia sovittiin maaliskuussa, mutta se avattiin uudelleen sen jälkeen, kun ravintola väitti Birenbaumin rikkoneen sovinnon ehtoja. Ravintolan mukaan ongelmana olivat Birenbaumin henkilökohtainen lausunto sekä hänen asianajajansa Rebekah Gilesin medialle lähettämät kommentit.

Tuomioistuimessa kuultiin, että Giles kuvaili sovintoa merkittäväksi voitoksi Birenbaumille ja Australian juutalaisyhteisölle. Ravintolan asianajajat väittivät toukokuun käsittelyssä, että Birenbaumin ja Gilesin lausunnot olivat koordinoitu yritys horjuttaa sovintoa ja ohjata julkista kertomusta.

Ravintolan asianajaja Matthew Richardson kuvaili lausuntoja oikeudessa voitonjulistuksiksi, joiden tarkoituksena oli hänen mukaansa peittää osapuolten yhteinen lausunto uutisvirrassa. Birenbaumin asianajaja Kieran Smark SC kiisti, että kommentit olisivat olleet ristiriidassa virallisen yhteislausunnon kanssa. Hän myös esitti, että Birenbaum oli oikeutettu kokemaan tulleensa vindikoiduksi, koska ravintola oli esittänyt julkisen anteeksipyynnön.
summary_bullets: Australian liittovaltion tuomioistuin katsoi Ofir Birenbaumin rikkoneen osia Cairo Takeaway -ravintolan kanssa tehdystä sovinnosta.
Kiista liittyi sovinnon jälkeen annettuihin lausuntoihin, joissa Birenbaum kuvasi tulleensa täysin oikeutetuksi.
Tapaus sai alkunsa Birenbaumin vierailusta sydneyläisravintolassa Daily Telegraphin toimittajien kanssa helmikuussa 2025.
